defects: Nontriviality hypothesis `(v i) ≠ 0` (function inequality) is not equivalent to `IsNontrivial`; since any absolute value satisfies v(1)=1, this is essentially vacuously true and fails to capture the required 'not the trivial absolute value' condition

Pairwise inequivalence hypothesis `v i ≠ v j` (mere function inequality) is strictly weaker than `¬(v i).IsEquiv (v j)`; two distinct-as-functions absolute values can still be equivalent (e.g. v and v^2), so the hypothesis fails to exclude cases where the theorem is false, making the produced statement not a faithful/true formalization
Uses `Fintype ι` instead of `Finite ι`, a data-vs-Prop mismatch (minor)

Conclusion drops the `WithAbs (v i)` construction entirely, so there is no topology on the codomain tied to the absolute values v_i; `Dense (Set.range ...)` on `ι → F` either fails to typecheck for a generic field F (no TopologicalSpace instance) or silently relies on an unrelated/default topology, losing the essential content that density is with respect to the product of the v_i-induced topologies

Conclusion uses `Set.range (fun x : F => fun i => x)` and `Dense` directly instead of `DenseRange (algebraMap F (Π i, WithAbs (v i)))`, losing the ring-homomorphism structure of the diagonal embedding tied to the correct topological instances
